ts volatility¶

volatility fits models in which the variance of a return series changes with time, in clusters of calm and turbulence. A model y_t = mean + e_t, e_t = sqrt(h_t) z_t lets the conditional variance h_t depend on past shocks and past variances: Garch and Garch11 (symmetric), Gjr (larger response to negative shocks) and Egarch (the logarithm of the variance, so no positivity constraints). MvGarch, MvGjr and MvEgarch fit several series with a constant conditional correlation.

All fits maximise the Gaussian likelihood. The pre-sample variance that starts the recursion is the mean squared residual, so the likelihood does not depend on the parameters being searched through its start-up value. The mean is the sample mean (when demean is on) and is held fixed during the search.

How To Call It¶

Fit a GARCH(1,1) to a series with volatility clustering and read the persistence, the fitted variances and a forecast.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
// Returns whose variance responds more to negative shocks: h = 0.05 + (0.05 + 0.20 * 1[r < 0]) r_prev^2 + 0.75 h_prev.
Series returns(int n) {
  std::vector<double> r(n);
  double h = 0.5, prev = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (t + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    const double z = (u - 0.5) * std::sqrt(12.0);
    h = 0.05 + (0.05 + (prev < 0 ? 0.20 : 0.0)) * prev * prev + 0.75 * h;
    r[t] = std::sqrt(h) * z;
    prev = r[t];
  }
  return pluss::make_series(r, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = returns(1000);
  const auto fit = ts::Garch11::fit_mle(y);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "omega " << fit.omega << ", alpha " << fit.alpha << ", beta " << fit.beta << ", persistence " << fit.alpha + fit.beta << "\n";
  show("forecast", fit.forecast(5, y));
}

Output

omega 0.0577, alpha 0.1464, beta 0.7303, persistence 0.8767
forecast         0.3267   0.3441   0.3594   0.3727   0.3845
